"I am fully endowed with the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and practice the three samādhis. He says:
"I am fully endowed with the practice of the *dhāraṇīs* and the various gates of *samādhi*. He says:
"I am fully endowed with the ten powers and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; I shall instruct sentient beings and purify the Buddha-lands."
To say, "I shall attain the wisdom of omniscience (sarvajñajñāna)," while remaining immersed in the conceit of a self, is what constitutes mundane prajñāpāramitā.
If a bodhisattva practices these worldly dharmas, they will enter into the conceit of a self.

However, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā), they have no notion of a self, no notion of giving, no notion of the object given, and no notion of a recipient; this is the practice of the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā) and constitutes the guidance for the giving of a bodhisattva mahāsattva.

When a bodhisattva practices ethical discipline, there is no perfection of ethical discipline; when practicing patience, there is no perfection of patience; when practicing diligence, there is no perfection of diligence; when practicing meditative concentration, there is no perfection of meditation; and when practicing great wisdom, there is no perfection of wisdom.
Practicing the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, there is nothing that exists and nothing upon which to rely.
Practicing great loving-kindness and great compassion, or practicing omniscience (sarvajñatā), likewise, there is nothing that exists and nothing upon which to lean.
“World-Honored One!
This is the practice of giving by a bodhisattva who practices the *prajñāpāramitā*, serving as their guide.
*The Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra of the Emitted Light*, Scroll Six.
The Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Scroll Seven.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Mokṣala of Khotan during the Western Jin Dynasty,
by Imperial Decree.
Chapter 33: On Guarding Practice. In the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Chapter Thirty-three: On Guarding Practice, the Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra:
“If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who receive this profound Prajñāpāramitā, and who recite, read, uphold, practice, and guard it.”
Kauśika! If this son of good family enters into the midst of battle,
his life-span shall never be cut short midway.
Swords, spears, or arrows shall never strike his body. Why is this?

Because this son of good family has, throughout the long night, practiced the six pāramitās; he has already subdued for himself the sword of lust and the thorns of hatred and delusion, and he further brings down lust, anger, and delusion upon others.
Having already subdued for oneself the sword-thrusts of false views, one further subdues the sword of false views for others;

furthermore, having subdued for oneself the sword-thrusts of habitual tendencies and the thorns of affection, one is likewise able to subdue the swords of habitual tendencies and affection for others.
Kauśika! For this reason, good sons and good daughters shall not be struck by spears, swords, blades, or arrows.
Furthermore, Kauśika!
Good son! Good daughter!

If a man or woman upholds, recites, and practices the Prajñāpāramitā while never departing from the mind of sarvajñatā (omniscience), they shall ultimately not be harmed by poison, ultimately not be harmed by sorcery, ultimately not be harmed by weapons, ultimately not be harmed by water, and ultimately not be harmed by fire; no evil matters whatsoever shall ever be able to afflict them.
Why is this? Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is the unsurpassed art.
Noble sons and noble daughters who study this art do not think of evil for themselves, nor do they think of evil toward others, nor do they think of evil toward both.
Why is this? Because there is neither self-existence nor existence of another; there is neither knowledge and vision, nor the five aggregates;
and extending upward to *sarvajñatā*, there is nothing that exists and nothing that can be attained.
Being without anything [to grasp], one does not think of one's own evil, nor does one think of the evil of others, nor does one think of the evil of both.
Until the attainment of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, one contemplates the intentions of sentient beings.
Why is this? Because they have studied this art.
All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past, future, and present have all, through this very art, personally attained unexcelled perfect enlightenment (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi).
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who study this Prajñāpāramitā, and who have already written it down and maintained it, then neither humans nor non-humans will ever be able to find an opportunity to harm them."

Why is this? Within the trichiliocosm and throughout the countless, incalculable lands of the ten directions, all the Cāturmahārājakāyika devas up to the Akaniṣṭha devas shall together protect these good men and good women who write down, uphold, and pay homage to the Prajñāpāramitā, honoring and serving them with reverence.
The merit of one who writes and maintains this is such as this.
If there is anyone who merely writes and maintains the *Prajñāpāramitā*, even if they do not recite, read, or practice it, that place is like sitting in a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).

Within the four directions, left and right, there may be animals or humans; as for those outside who might wish to come and harm them—whether they be humans or non-humans—they shall ultimately find no opportunity to do so.
Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past attained Buddhahood therein;
and all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the future and present shall likewise attain Buddhahood therein.
Having attained the path of Buddhahood, they cause all sentient beings to be without fear or dread.
Being free from fear and dread, all receive the blessings of gods and humans, and are established in the Three Vehicles to bring them across to liberation.
Why is this so? Kauśika!
This Prajñāpāramitā is like the ground of the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), providing protection for all.
"One should pay homage and make offerings of famous flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incenses, silken banners, flower canopies, standards, pennants, and musical performances.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

If there are good sons or good daughters who, having written down the Prajñāpāramitā, take up the scroll and make offerings to it with famous flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incense, silken banners, flower canopies, flags, and music—thus performing such offerings.

If, after the Parinirvāṇa of the World-Honored One, one takes up his relics and makes offerings to them with famous flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incense, silk banners, flower canopies, standards, pennants, and music.
"If one makes such offerings, which brings forth greater merit?
The Buddha told Śakra Devānām Indra: "Kauśika!..."
I now ask you; answer as you see fit according to my question.
What do you think? It is by means of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, having attained sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), that these marks and signs were acquired.
"From what has this been learned?
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
I have heard that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, having attained sarvajñatā and perfected the marks and signs, acquired these through training in the Prajñāpāramitā.
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is, Kauśika!"
It is not because of this physical body that one is called a Tathāgata; rather, it is because of having attained the wisdom of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) that one becomes a Tathāgata.
This *sarvajñatā* is born from within the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Thus it is, Kauśika! This body of the Tathāgata is the dwelling-place of the wisdom of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge).
Because the Tathāgata, by means of this dwelling, has attained sarvajñatā, it is therefore called the dwelling-place of the wisdom of sarvajñatā.
After my parinirvāṇa, the śarīras shall be honored in this manner.

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family writes out the Prajñāpāramitā, recites, reads, explains, studies, maintains, and practices it, and honors the scripture with famous flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incenses, silk banners, flower canopies, flags, pennants, and music, and pays homage with reverence; [the merit shall be as great as that].
One who makes such an offering has already made an offering to *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge). Thus it is, Kauśika!

For this reason, good sons and good daughters who receive, uphold, recite, read, and explain the *prajñāpāramitā* should guard and practice it; they should honor the scripture with named flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incenses, silken banners, flower canopies, flags, pennants, and music, and they should pay homage to it with reverence.

If, after his parinirvāṇa, one makes offerings to his relics by establishing them in a securely situated stūpa, adorning it with various flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incenses, silken banners, canopies, flags, and musical performances.

If there are good sons or good daughters who write down and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, reciting, memorizing, guarding, honoring, and making offerings to it with famous flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incense, silken banners, flower canopies, flags, and musical performances—making such offerings as these.
The merit of this is greater than that of making offerings to the śarīra. Why is this?
Because it is from within this that the śarīra is produced.

The emptiness of the internal and external, as well as the emptiness of existence and non-existence, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all arise from within this.
All gateways to samādhi and gateways to dhāraṇī likewise arise from within this.
The transformation and guidance of sentient beings and the purification of Buddha-lands also arise from within it.

The householder’s accomplishments, the accomplishment of physical form, the accomplishment of wealth, the accomplishment of retinues, and great loving-kindness and great compassion—all these arise from within it. The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s [attainments] all arise from this.
The Kṣatriya caste, the Brāhmaṇa caste, and the castes of great clans and elders, from the Four Heavenly Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, are all born from within it.
From the stage of srotāpanna up to arhat, pratyekabuddha, bodhisattva, the Buddha, the Tathāgata, and even sarvajñā, all are born from within it.
At that time, Śakra Devānām-Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Those people of Jambudvīpa who do not make offerings to, serve, or revere the Prajñāpāramitā are individuals who do not know its sublimity or what it is that should be honored.”
The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:
"Kauśika, what do you think?
How many people in Jambudvīpa do you know who have faith in the Buddha, faith in the Dharma, and faith in the Saṃgha of bhikṣus?"
"How many people harbor doubts regarding the Three Honored Ones?
And how many people revere the Three Honored Ones?
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Those who have faith and rely upon the Buddha, rely upon the Dharma, and rely upon the Saṅgha of bhikṣus are but few indeed.
The Buddha said:

"Kauśika, what do you think? How many sentient beings in Jambudvīpa are capable of attaining the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the three gates of liberation, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditations, the six supernormal powers, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, and the four kinds of unimpeded wisdom?"
In Jambudvīpa, how many sentient beings have extinguished the three doubts and are destined for the stage of Srotāpanna?
How many sentient beings have attenuated the three impurities and are destined for the stage of Sakṛdāgāmin?
How many sentient beings will sever their five doubts and become *anāgāmins*?
How many sentient beings will, having completed the five higher stages, become *arhats*?
And how many sentient beings will give rise to the path of a *pratyekabuddha*?
"How many sentient beings have resolved their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Very few sentient beings are destined to attain the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and the state of a Samyaksaṃbuddha;
they are but very few. The Buddha said to Śakra-devānām-indra: "It is so, Kauśika!"
Sentient beings are exceedingly numerous, yet those who give rise to the aspiration for the Way are but few. Why is this?
It is because in previous lives they did not see the Buddha, did not hear the Dharma, and did not recognize the Sangha of bhikṣus.

They do not practice giving, nor do they maintain the precepts or guard the moral code; they do not exercise patience, nor do they apply diligence. They have not heard of dhyāna, nor have they heard of the prajñāpāramitā; they have neither heard of internal and external emptiness nor of the emptiness of existence and non-existence. They have neither heard of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment nor of the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, nor do they reflect upon them. They have neither heard of samādhi nor of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), nor do they bring such matters to mind.
For this reason, Kauśika, you should know that only a few sentient beings believe in the Three Honored Ones.
Among them, even fewer sentient beings resolve their minds toward the path of a pratyekabuddha; and among those, even fewer still practice the bodhisattva path.
Although there are a few sentient beings who practice the bodhisattva path, those who wish to reach *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* are even fewer still, Kauśika!

In this regard, with my Buddha-eye, I see that among the incalculable, asāṃkhyeya sentient beings in the ten directions who practice for anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, only one or two abide on the stage of avaivartika because they do not depart from the *upāya-kauśalya* of the *prajñā-pāramitā*;
many fall into the paths of the arhat or pratyekabuddha because they have departed from the *upāya-kauśalya* of the *prajñā-pāramitā*.

Therefore, Kauśika! A son of good family or a daughter of good family who wishes to set forth toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* should receive and uphold the *prajñāpāramitā*; they should recite, read, contemplate, practice, and maintain this *prajñāpāramitā*. Having written it down, they should honor it with incense, flowers, banners, streamers, silken cloths, and canopies; and for all other meritorious deeds that enter into the *prajñāpāramitā*, they should likewise receive and uphold them, as well as recite, study, contemplate, and maintain their practice.
What are the merits that enter the Prajñāpāramitā? They are: giving, morality, patience, diligence, and single-mindedness;

internal and external emptiness, the emptiness of existence, and the emptiness of non-existence; the various gates of samādhi and the gates of dhāraṇī; the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, great loving-kindness, and great compassion; and all other immeasurable Buddha-dharmas—all these enter the Prajñāpāramitā.
Furthermore, you should also learn to uphold, recite, maintain, and keep in mind the matters contained therein.
Why is this so, Kauśika?
These good sons and good daughters should understand this:

"When the Tathāgatas were originally practicing the bodhisattva path, they also studied the *prajñāpāramitā*, and they also practiced the *dhyānapāramitā*, the *vīryapāramitā*, the *kṣāntipāramitā*, the *śīlapāramitā*, and the *dānapāramitā*. From internal and external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) up to the emptiness of existence and non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), through the various gates of samādhi and the gates of dhāraṇī, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharma*) and great loving-kindness and great compassion—we ourselves shall likewise receive and study all these countless other qualities of the Buddhas."
That which we revere and honor—the Prajñāpāramitā and all the Buddha-dharmas—is entirely the teaching of the Tathāgatas.

From the teachings of the Pratyekabuddhas, Arhats, Anāgāmins, Sakṛdāgāmins, and Srotāpannas, up to those of Sarvajña, all are perfected through training in the Prajñāpāramitā; they cross from this shore to the other shore.

"Kauśika! Whether the Tathāgata is in the world or has entered parinirvāṇa, good sons and good daughters should all reverently honor and serve these six pāramitās, and they should also honor and serve sarvajñatā (all-knowledge)."
Why is this? This Prajñāpāramitā is the protector of all bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas; humans and devas alike rely upon this Prajñāpāramitā to attain peace and security.

Kauśika! If there are good men or good women who, after the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, take up his relics and erect a stūpa made of the seven precious jewels forty *li* in height, and throughout their entire lifespan take refuge in and serve it, making offerings such as celestial flowers, celestial incense, celestial powdered incense, celestial silk flower-canopies, celestial robes, and celestial curtains.
"Would that merit not be great?
Śakra Devānām Indra said:
"World-Honored One!"
"Very much, very much! The Buddha said,

"It is not equal to a son or daughter of good family who receives and practices the Prajñāpāramitā, who copies, maintains, recites, reads, and upholds the sūtra scrolls, never departing from the mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), and further adds offerings of famous flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incenses, banners, flags, and flower canopies."
The merit thereof will be manifold and beyond calculation.
Furthermore, Kauśika! Set aside this single stūpa made of the seven treasures.

If a son or daughter of good family were to collect relics and erect stupas made of the seven precious substances, filling the entirety of Jambudvīpa, each forty li in height, and perform offerings and services with celestial flowers, celestial incense, celestial powdered incense, celestial silk banners, celestial canopies, celestial robes, and celestial curtains—performing such offerings as these.
"Would that merit not be great?
Śakra-devānām-indra replied,
"It would be very great, indeed very great!"
"World-Honored One!
The Buddha said:
"It is not as [meritorious] as when a son or daughter of good family makes offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā; their merit is many times greater."
Furthermore, Kauśika! Let us set aside the matter of building stūpas for Jambudvīpa.

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to take up relics and erect stūpas made of the seven precious substances filling the four continents, and make offerings as previously described;
It is not equal to the merit of a son or daughter of good family who makes offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā; their merit is many times greater.
Let alone these four continents.

Kauśika! If there were good men or good women who, having taken up relics, erected stupas made of the seven precious substances filling a small chiliocosm, and made offerings to them as previously described;
Setting aside for a moment the seven-jeweled stupas built within these small thousandfold world-systems,
if a son or daughter of good family were to take up the śarīra relics and erect seven-jeweled stupas filling a medium thousandfold world-system, and make offerings to them as previously described.
Setting aside for a moment the seven-jeweled stūpas constructed within those intermediate thousandfold world systems,
if a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to take up the relics and erect seven-jeweled stūpas filling a great trichiliocosm, and were to make offerings as described above.
It is not equal to the merit of these sons and daughters of good family who make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā; their merit is many times greater.
Kausika! Furthermore, let us set aside the seven-jeweled stūpas erected throughout this trichiliocosm.

If the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system were filled with people, and each individual were to erect a stupa made of the seven treasures and make offerings as described above, it would not equal the merit of this son or daughter of good family who makes offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā; their merit would be many times greater.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying: “So it is, so it is!
World-Honored One!”
"To make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā is to have already made offerings to all the Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present.
The Buddha said:

"Suppose that as many sentient beings as would fill the lands of the Ganges-sand in the eastern direction were to each, after the parinirvāṇa of a Buddha, take his relics and erect stūpas of the seven treasures filling those lands; and suppose they were to make offerings as described above, from kalpa to kalpa, for even more than a kalpa, until the end of their lifespans."
"What do you think, Kauśika!
Would that person not plant even more merit?
Śakra Devānām Indra replied:
“Very much, very much!

The Buddha said, “It is not equal to the merit obtained by a son or daughter of good family who makes offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā by copying and maintaining the sūtra scrolls, reciting, reading, and practicing them, and by offering them famous incense, unguent incense, blended incense, silken banners, flowers, and canopies; the latter obtains far more merit.”
Why is this so? Kauśika!
All wholesome dharmas are contained within the Prajñāpāramitā.
What are the wholesome dharmas?

They are the five precepts, the ten wholesome paths of action, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, the four formless attainments, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the three gates of liberation, the four truths, the six supernormal powers, the eight liberations, the nine successive meditations, the six pāramitās, from internal and external emptiness up to the emptiness of existence and non-existence, the various gates of samādhi, the gates of dhāraṇī, the ten powers of a Buddha, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the four unhindered wisdoms, great loving-kindness and great compassion, the matters of the path, and the matters of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge). These constitute the Dharma teachings of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
All Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, and all Tathāgatas of the past, future, and present have studied and perfected themselves within this Prajñāpāramitā, thereby crossing over to the other shore.
Chapter 34: On Offerings. The Mahāprajñāpāramitā, Chapter Thirty-Four: On Offerings. The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying: "It is so, Kauśika!"

Good sons and good daughters who make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā, who copy and uphold its scrolls, and who receive, study, recite, contemplate, practice, and maintain it—if they can further make offerings with all their might using famous flowers, powdered incense, liquid incense, blended incense, silken banners, flower parasols, and all manner of standards and pennants—the merit they obtain will be immeasurable, inconceivable, and beyond limit.
Such are the attainments of these good sons and good daughters.
Why is this? Because all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas are born from within the Prajñāpāramitā.
Sarvajñā (all-knowledge) and the five pāramitās are all born from the prajñāpāramitā;
from internal and external emptiness up to the emptiness of existence and non-existence, all are born from the prajñāpāramitā;

the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the five eyes of a Tathāgata—which teach sentient beings and purify buddha-fields—as well as the wisdom of the path and the wisdom of sarvajñā, are all born from the prajñāpāramitā.
The paths of the Śrāvaka, the Pratyekabuddha, and the unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment of the Buddha-vehicle all arise from the Prajñāpāramitā.
Thus it is, Kauśika!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who write out the *Prajñāpāramitā*, and who uphold its scrolls, study, receive, recite, contemplate, guard, practice, and cultivate it, further adding offerings of famous flowers, powdered incense, silken banners, canopies, and the like—their merit and blessings shall exceed those of the previously mentioned offerings to the stūpas made of the seven treasures containing relics by hundreds of thousands of millions, billions of times; it is so vast that it cannot be measured and is beyond all analogy.
Why is this? If the Prajñāpāramitā exists in the world, the Three Jewels will never be severed;
if the Prajñāpāramitā does not exist in the world, the Three Jewels will then be severed.

When the Prajñāpāramitā abides in the world, one then knows that there are the merits of the ten precepts, the four immeasurables, the four dhyānas, and the four formless concentrations; the six pāramitās, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and the wisdom of omniscience (sarvajñājñāna). One then knows that there are the kṣatriya caste, the brāhmaṇa caste, and the castes of great clans and elders; one then knows that there are the Four Heavenly Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; one then knows that there are the paths from srotāpanna up to arhat, as well as the path of the pratyekabuddha; one then knows that there is the path of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva; one then knows that there is the unsurpassed wisdom of a Buddha; one then knows that there is the turning of the wheel of Dharma; and one then knows that there is the teaching and transforming of sentient beings and the purification of buddha-fields.

Chapter 35: The Chapter on Upholding (Dhāraṇī-parivarta). At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings of the trichiliocosm, as well as all the devaputras up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, spoke to Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:
"O Benevolent One!"

When one upholds the Prajñāpāramitā, recites it, studies and contemplates it, and practices it, and when one makes offerings to those who recite, study, and contemplate it, all other evil dharmas shall be completely extinguished, and all virtuous merits shall arise in full abundance.
Those who receive and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā will increase the hosts of devas and diminish the hosts of asuras.

The Dharma of the Three Jewels shall never be severed. Because the Buddha-Dharma is not severed, the six pāramitās, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha shall all appear in the world; there shall be those who practice the bodhisattva path, and there shall be the teachings of the three vehicles.
The Buddha told Kauśika:
"You should receive, uphold, recite, read, maintain, remember, and practice the Prajñāpāramitā. Why is this?"
If the asuras assemble their hosts, desiring to give rise to evil intent and wage war against the Trāyastriṃśa devas,
Kauśika! If you should recite and contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā, then as soon as the asuras conceive such an intention, it shall be extinguished immediately and shall not reach its conclusion.

Kauśika! If any sons of the gods or daughters of the gods in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven, when their merit is exhausted and their lifespan is about to end, are on the verge of falling back down, you should recite and expound the Prajñāpāramitā for them.

These devas and celestial maidens shall not go to other realms of existence; by virtue of the merit of the sound of the *prajñāpāramitā*, they will immediately be reborn again in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.
These devas and humans will be reborn in their original abodes and shall no longer fall away. Why is this?
Because the merit of the sound of the Prajñāpāramitā is great.
Kauśika! If a son of good family or a daughter of good family, or any devaputra or devakanyā, should hear the sound of this Prajñāpāramitā even as it passes once through their ears;
by virtue of that single hearing, such a person shall, after a long time, certainly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, never again having any doubt.
Why is this? Kauśika!
Because all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions in the past—
Anābhibhū! It is because the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and his assembly of disciples all attain parinirvāṇa in the nirvana without remainder from within this Prajñāpāramitā.
All Tathāgatas of the ten directions, both those yet to come and those present now, have all attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi from within the Prajñāpāramitā.

Why is this? All thirty-seven factors of enlightenment are born from within the Prajñāpāramitā; the dharmas of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, and the Buddha—all are born from within the Prajñāpāramitā.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā is the ultimate great art; the Prajñāpāramitā is the unsurpassed art; the Prajñāpāramitā is the peerless art.”
Why is this so? World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā has already cast off all unwholesome dharmas and maintains the root of all wholesome dharmas.
The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:
"So it is, Kauśika! This Prajñāpāramitā is the supreme art, the unsurpassed and peerless art."
Why is this? Because all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi by means of this method;
likewise, all the Buddhas of the future and those of the present shall also attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi by means of this method.

Why is this? It is because by means of this artifice, the world comes to know the virtues of the ten wholesome paths, the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments; the six pāramitās, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. It knows the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), the fixed position of phenomena (dharmasthiti), and the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi). It knows the Tathāgata, it knows the five eyes, it knows the path of the srotāpanna, it knows the paths of the arhat and the pratyekabuddha, it knows the paths of the bodhisattva and the Buddha, and it knows sarvajñā and sarvajñajñāna.

It is because of the bodhisattvas that the virtue of the ten wholesome paths of action is manifested in the world, and even the Tathāgata and sarvajñatā (all-knowledge) are manifested in the world; all these manifestations exist due to the causes and conditions of the bodhisattvas' coming and going.
Kauśika! It is like the moon, which by reason of its coming and going removes the darkness of the world and illuminates the constellations.
In this same way, Kauśika!

The Bodhisattva is born from wholesome conduct and equal practice; he is born from the merit of the ten wholesome paths of action; he is born from the wisdom of sarvajñā (all-knowledge); he is born from the dharma of non-arising.
Kauśika! You should know that all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are born from the *prajñāpāramitā*.

The five *pāramitās* practiced by bodhisattvas, as well as internal and external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) and the emptiness of existence and non-existence (*abhāva-svabhāva-śūnyatā*), the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (*saptatriṃśad-bodhipakṣa-dharmāḥ*), and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha (*āveṇika-buddhadharmāḥ*), do not lead them to realize the stage of the śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha; rather, they instruct sentient beings and purify the buddha-fields.

"If one wishes to achieve the fulfillment of a Buddha-field, the fulfillment of bodhisattvas, and the fulfillment of the attainment of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), all of these arise from the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Furthermore, Kauśika!"

If there are good sons or good daughters who receive and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, and who recite, read, study, and practice its teachings, they will immediately attain the virtues of the present life and shall also attain the virtues that transcend the world.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"What are the virtues attained in the present life by good men and good women?
The Buddha said:

"One who practices the Prajñāpāramitā shall never die from poison, nor shall they ever die by an untimely or violent death through water or fire; they shall all live out their full natural lifespan before passing away."
If there are matters concerning local officials and one goes before them, in the end no one will be able to take advantage of one.
Why is this? It is entirely due to the majestic spiritual power of the recitation of the Prajñāpāramitā.

If these good sons or good daughters go before a king, a crown prince, or the various ministers, their speech will accord with the minds of the king, the crown prince, and all the ministers, such that there are none who do not rejoice.
Why is this? It is because these good sons and good daughters practice great kindness and great compassion, directing the four immeasurable minds toward all sentient beings.
This constitutes their merit in the present life.
“What is it to be fully endowed with the virtues that transcend the world?
The Buddha said:
“It is never to be separated from these ten meritorious virtues of good conduct, nor ever to be separated from the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and...”
The four dhyānas of emptiness, the six pāramitās, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha—
he never departs from these dharmas at the beginning, nor does he ultimately give rise to birth in the three evil realms;
his physical form is complete, all his faculties are fully endowed, he never takes birth in a poor household, he never takes birth in the house of a craftsman, nor does he take birth elsewhere.
Within the households of ordinary beings, one shall always be fully endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Being;

in whatever Buddha-lands one is born, one shall always be born by transformation; never shall one be separated from the supernatural powers and vows of a bodhisattva, desiring to travel from one Buddha-land to another to reverently serve and honor the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and constantly desiring to hear and receive [their teachings].
This is the supreme dharma of all Buddhas, intended to transform sentient beings and purify Buddha-fields.

Therefore, Kauśika, good sons and good daughters who receive, uphold, recite, read, and contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā should guard and practice it, never departing from the mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), until they achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, never interrupting this course from the very beginning.
"This is the merit for transcending the world in future ages.

36. Chapter Thirty-Six: Dispatching Heterodox Teachers. *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, Chapter Thirty-Six: Dispatching Heterodox Teachers. At that time, there was a heterodox teacher who came to where the Buddha was, seeking to find an opportunity to challenge him.
Śakra Devānām Indra thought to himself:
"Today these various heterodox practitioners have come, desiring to slander the Buddha and to cut off the Prajñāpāramitā midway."
"As I have received the Prajñāpāramitā from the Buddha, I shall recite and keep it in mind.
Śakra Devānām-indra then immediately recited the Prajñāpāramitā.
When various heterodox practitioners who wished to come and destroy the *prajñāpāramitā* saw [the Buddha], they circumambulated the Buddha from afar once and returned by the same path.
At that time, Śāriputra thought to himself:
"Why have these groups of heterodox practitioners circumambulated the Buddha from afar once and then returned by the same path?"
The Buddha, knowing what Śāriputra was thinking, addressed Śāriputra, saying:
"It is because Śakra Devānām Indra recited and contemplated the Prajñāpāramitā that the followers of other paths circumambulated the Buddha from afar once and then returned by the way they came."
The Buddha said, "These heterodox practitioners have not come to the Buddha’s presence with even a single virtuous thought; they have merely come with hostile intent to seek out the Buddha's faults.
The Buddha then addressed Śāriputra:

"If, when one is reciting the *Prajñāpāramitā*, whether gods, worldly humans, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, or followers of other teachings should come with hostile intent seeking to find fault, they will ultimately be unable to find any opportunity."

Why is this? It is because the Four Heavenly Kings, the sons of gods, and even the sons of gods up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, as well as the disciples and the bodhisattvas throughout this trichiliocosm, uphold the Prajñāpāramitā.
Why is this? Because these, too, are all born from within the Prajñāpāramitā.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!

The Tathāgatas, their assemblies of disciples, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and spirits in all the lands as numerous as the sands along the banks of the Ganges in the eastern direction—all these uphold the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Why is this? Because all these arise from the Prajñāpāramitā.
At that time, Māra Pāpīyān thought to himself:

"Now the Buddha is assembled with his fourfold assembly of disciples, as well as the sons of the gods of the desire realm and the sons of the gods of the form realm; among them there shall be those who receive the prediction of becoming Bodhisattvas, and they will certainly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Now I shall go to where the Buddha is and cut off his path.
Thereupon, Pāpīyas manifested himself as four kinds of military forces and approached the place where the Buddha was.
At that time, Śakra-devānām-indra thought to himself:
"Today, the Māra will lead his fourfold army to the place where the Buddha is; this is an army conjured by Māra.

The splendor with which these fourfold armies are adorned is such that King Bimbisāra does not possess it, nor does the King of Śrāvastī, nor do the Śākyas, nor do the various elders of the Sūrpāraka region."
"These four kinds of troops conjured by Māra are the work of Māra Pāpīyān, who throughout the long night has constantly sought out the Buddha's shortcomings and harassed sentient beings.
I would now rather silently recite and contemplate the Prajñāpāramitā."
Śakra Devānām Indra then concentrated his mind and gradually recited the Prajñāpāramitā;
at that time, Māra Pāpīyas also gradually retreated and departed.
At that time, the sons of the gods from the Four Great Kings and the sons of the gods from Akaniṣṭha manifested celestial flowers in the void and scattered them over the Buddha.
Then the sons of the gods simultaneously exclaimed:
"May the Prajñāpāramitā remain long in Jambudvīpa, so that the people of Jambudvīpa may always receive, uphold, and practice the Prajñāpāramitā."
If the Prajñāpāramitā endures for a long time, the Buddha will also abide for a long time and there will be no time of his extinction.
If the Buddha abides for a long time, the Dharma shall likewise endure for a long time.
If that which accords with the Dharma remains for a long time, the community of bhikṣus will constantly appear in the world.

In this way, the Three Jewels shall never suffer interruption; likewise, the Prajñāpāramitā shall also remain for a long time within the trichiliocosm, and it shall be the same in the buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions.
The Prajñāpāramitā is the supreme and most excellent among all the practices of Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

Any son of good family or daughter of good family who receives, maintains, and writes out the scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā will, in whatever direction or location they are, be the most honored and become a source of illumination.
"You should know that this place is already free from darkness; it is the most honored among all such places.
The Buddha said to Śakra Devānām Indra: "So it is, Kauśika!"
You should know that this is the most honored among all assemblies. Furthermore,
Kauśika, this Prajñāpāramitā is not only the most honored among humans, but it is also the most honored in the heavens.
At that time, the sons of the gods manifested celestial flowers and scattered them over the Buddha; they all raised their voices simultaneously and said:
"If there are good men or good women who receive, uphold, recite, and study the Prajñāpāramitā, Māra and the gods of Māra shall never be able to find an opportunity against them."
"World-Honored One,
we too shall protect these good men and good women. Why is this?"
"We regard these sons and daughters of good family as we regard the World-Honored One.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

These good sons and good daughters, who recite, contemplate, and uphold this Prajñāpāramitā by virtue of having cultivated immeasurable roots of goodness, have brought this about through the merit they performed during the time of past Buddhas.
These good sons and good daughters have been brought here by having seen immeasurable Buddhas, and by following along with spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra). Why is this?
Those who wish to attain *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) should seek it from the *prajñāpāramitā*;
those who wish to attain the *prajñāpāramitā* should likewise seek it from *sarvajñatā*.
For this reason, the Prajñāpāramitā is itself sarvajñatā, and sarvajñatā is itself the Prajñāpāramitā; these are one and the same, without duality.
The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:
"So it is, Kauśika! All-sagacity (sarvajñatā), all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas—all these are born from the Prajñāpāramitā."
For what reason? Kauśika!
It is because of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge)!
“Prajñāpāramitā is but a single dharma, for there are no two. Chapter Thirty-Seven:
Non-duality, the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Chapter Thirty-Seven on Non-duality. At that time, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Yes, World-Honored One!”
The Blessed One did not initially praise the five perfections, nor did he praise the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; he praised only the perfection of wisdom.
"Why is this? The Buddha told Ānanda:
"The Prajñāpāramitā is the most honored among the five pāramitās and the eighteen dharmas of a Buddha."
"What do you think, Ānanda?
If one does not practice giving for the sake of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), can that dānapāramitā (perfection of giving) truly be praised? He replied:
"No, World-Honored One!
Would one not praise the *prajñāpāramitā* even if it were not for the sake of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) regarding morality, patience, diligence, single-mindedness, and wisdom?"
"No, World-Honored One," Ānanda replied to the Buddha.
"How is it that giving, when directed toward *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), constitutes the perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) up to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*)?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"When giving is non-dual with respect to *sarvajñatā*, this is the perfection of giving; it acts without production and without dependence."
To practice giving for the sake of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) is the perfection of generosity (*dānapāramitā*), being without production and without reliance on thought.
That *sarvajñatā* is non-dual is the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying,
“How is it that mindfulness is non-dual, such that giving corresponds to sarvajñatā?
The Buddha said:
"In the five aggregates there is no duality, and in the attainment of the Way there is likewise no duality.
Why is it that in the five aggregates there is no duality, and in the attainment of the Way there is likewise no duality?"
The five aggregates are empty of their own nature. Why is this?
The five aggregates and the various pāramitās are but a single dharma; there are no two dharmas.
Regarding the Path as well, there is but one dharma; there are not two.
Therefore, Ānanda, among the five pāramitās, the prajñāpāramitā is the most honored, and even up to sarvajñatā, it is likewise the most honored among them.
For example, just as when the seeds of the five grains are sown within the great earth, they grow in accordance with the seasons;
so too, the Prajñāpāramitā is the earth, from which all the pāramitās, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and everything up to sarvajñatā are born.
Sarvajñā (all-knowledge) is born from the *prajñāpāramitā*.
Likewise, the five *pāramitās* are also born from Sarvajñā. Therefore, Ānanda!
"The Prajñāpāramitā is the guide of the five pāramitās;
from the five pāramitās up to the eighteen dharmas of a Buddha, all follow it.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“The merit of the Prajñāpāramitā praised by the World-Honored One is inexhaustible.

Furthermore, for good sons and good daughters who receive and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā—whether they recite, read, study, contemplate, maintain, practice, honor, or make offerings to it—their merit is likewise inexhaustible.”
Because they uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, the ten wholesome paths appear in the world;
the four dhyānas, the four immeasurables, and the four formless attainments, up to the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, all appear in the world.

Because they practice the Prajñāpāramitā, they come to know the existence of the Kṣatriyas, Brahmins, and great clans of householders; they come to know the Four Heavenly Kings up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; and they come to know the existence of the path of the Srotāpanna up to the paths of the Arhat, Pratyekabuddha, Bodhisattva, and the Buddha.
The Buddha told Kauśika:
"The merit of those good men and good women who receive, uphold, recite, practice, and make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā, as I have described it, is not yet exhausted."
The merit of those who uphold, recite, practice, and make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā is incalculable and immeasurable. Why is this so?

These sons and daughters of good family who practice the *prajñāpāramitā* shall attain immeasurable nature of precepts, and attain immeasurable natures of samādhi, wisdom, liberation, and the vision and knowledge of liberation; their minds shall never depart from the mind of *sarvajñatā*.
These sons and daughters of good family shall all attain these incalculable merits. Kausika,
you should know that those sons and daughters of good family who practice the Prajñāpāramitā act as the successors of the Buddha and shall never be separated from sarvajñatā (all-knowledge).

Kauśika! As for the nature of the precepts, samādhi, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation possessed by śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas—if one compares those who maintain these five natures with the fivefold nature of these good sons and good daughters, the latter’s merit is a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and hundreds of billions of times greater; their merit is most supreme, such that nothing can serve as a metaphor for it.
Why is this? Kauśika!

It is because the minds of these sons and daughters of good family have already transcended those of the arhats and pratyekabuddhas; from the very beginning, they have not even entertained the aspiration for the state of an arhat or a pratyekabuddha.

Kauśika! If there are those who write down, uphold, study, recite, and keep in mind the Prajñāpāramitā, and those who make offerings of flowers, incense, silken canopies, and parasols, I shall always praise and speak of the virtues of these good men and good women in this life, in future lives, and throughout the ultimate end.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I, too, shall constantly protect these good men and good women who practice the Prajñāpāramitā, ensuring that their minds do not depart from the mind of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge)."
The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:

“When these sons and daughters of good family recite and expound the Prajñāpāramitā, hundreds of thousands of myriads of devas will all go to where these sons and daughters of good family are, and with palms joined, they will listen to and receive the Prajñāpāramitā.”
These devaputras shall further empower these good men and good women with their majestic spiritual power, causing them to quickly attain understanding and increasing their wisdom and eloquence.
This constitutes the merit that these good men and good women obtain in the present life.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

When these sons and daughters of good family preach the Prajñāpāramitā among the fourfold assembly of disciples, they will never feel weary or indolent, and no one will ever be able to perceive them as having such states; how much less could anyone wish to disparage or revile them?"
Why is this? Because they are protected by the Prajñāpāramitā.
The Prajñāpāramitā is that which discerns all dharmas.
What is meant by discrimination? It is to distinguish:

"This is the supramundane, this is the mundane; this is wholesome, this is unwholesome; this is outflow-free, this is with outflows; this is complete, this is incomplete; this is the Dharma of the śrāvakas, this is the Dharma of the pratyekabuddhas, this is the Buddha-Dharma. This is what constitutes discrimination.

Why is this? Because these sons and daughters of good family have already dwelled in internal and external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) as well as the emptiness of existence and non-existence (*bhāvābhāva-śūnyatā*).
Since they employ the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*) without deficiency, they do not perceive anyone who could bring deficiency to their perfection of wisdom.
For one who thus upholds the Prajñāpāramitā, no one shall be able to find an opportunity to harm them. Furthermore, Kauśika,
when a son of good family or a daughter of good family practices the Prajñāpāramitā in this manner and maintains it in this manner, their mind will never grow weary, nor will they ever be terrified.
Why is this? Because these good men and good women shall never see any sign of fear or indolence.
This constitutes the merit and virtue of these good men and good women in the present life.
"Furthermore, Kauśika!

If there are sons or daughters of good family who receive and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, making offerings of incense, flowers, banners, pennants, silken canopies, and parasols—those sons or daughters of good family who perform such offerings will be respected and loved by their parents; they will be honored by their brothers, kinsmen, friends, and associates; and all the Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Buddhas of the ten directions will together love and respect them."
These good sons and good daughters will be loved and respected by the people of the world, as well as by the devas and asuras.

They will practice the six pāramitās without interruption, never being separated from internal and external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) and the emptiness of existence and non-existence (*bhāva-abhāva-śūnyatā*), never being separated from the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and never being separated from the gates of various samādhis and dhāraṇīs. They will never cease their practice of the bodhisattva’s supernormal powers, teaching sentient beings and purifying buddha-fields; their strength shall be sufficient to subdue external critics.
Kauśika! These are the merits for a son of good family or a daughter of good family who receives and practices the Prajñāpāramitā in this life and in future lives. Kauśika!

Good sons and good daughters who write out the Prajñāpāramitā and who hold its scrolls and recite them will have all the Cāturmahārājika devas from within the trichiliocosm come to the place where these good sons and good daughters dwell. Having listened to and received the Prajñāpāramitā, they will pay homage with reverence and then depart.

From the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, all those devas who practice the bodhisattva path will come to where these good men and good women are, to hear and receive the Prajñāpāramitā; having paid homage and shown them reverence, they will depart.

The Four Heavenly Kings of the ten directions, the Akaniṣṭha devas, as well as the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas, all came to behold the Prajñāpāramitā, prostrating, making offerings, serving, and paying homage to it.
These good sons and good daughters should understand this:
"This is the gift of Dharma.

Within this trichiliocosm and throughout all the lands of the ten directions, from the Cāturmahārājika devas and their sons up to the sons of the gods in the Akaniṣṭha heaven—those who practice the bodhisattva path—all shall together protect these good sons and good daughters who practice the prajñāpāramitā; no evil or malevolent harms shall find an opportunity against them, except for those resulting from their own past karma.
Thus it is, Kauśika!
These sons and daughters of good family obtain blessings in the present life.

As for those devaputras who wish to come to where these sons and daughters of good family dwell, it is because they desire to achieve *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and they desire to rescue and protect sentient beings, to bring peace and security to sentient beings, and to cause sentient beings to find joy.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How should these sons and daughters of good family know that the Four Heavenly Kings of the ten directions and all the gods up to the Akaniṣṭha Heaven have come to where the Prajñāpāramitā is?”
"When these good men and good women respectfully receive, uphold, and pay homage [to this teaching], how shall they know that it is so?
The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:

"If these good men and good women see an extraordinary color or pure radiance, they should know that it is because the devas and humans have come to listen to and receive the Prajñāpāramitā, paying homage with reverence."

Kauśika! When these sons and daughters of good family smell a wondrous and extraordinary fragrance that they have never smelled before, you should know that it is because the great and venerable devas have come to listen to and receive the Prajñāpāramitā, paying homage with reverence.
Kauśika! These sons and daughters of good family should always maintain purity and take joy therein.

Because they take joy in their purity, all the devas will be greatly delighted; they will come to where these sons and daughters of good family are to hear and receive the Prajñāpāramitā, to serve them, and to pay them homage.

When this Great Honored Deva arrives, all the minor devas, ghosts, and spirits of little spiritual power in this place will flee, for they are unable to withstand the majestic power of this Honored Deva.
Because these various honored devas have come, these sons and daughters of good family shall all be free from manifold difficulties.

Wherever these sons and daughters of good family dwell, they should always maintain a pure and clean environment, lighting lamps, burning incense, hanging silk banners, flowers, and canopies, and constantly making pure offerings with immeasurable adornments.
These good sons and good daughters will never harbor a mind of weariness; their physical consciousness will be light and agile, and they will always attain peace and stability.
Whether lying down or rising, they will be at ease and never experience evil dreams;
they shall see no other dreams, but only dream of seeing the Buddha, hearing the Dharma, beholding the community of bhikṣus, and seeing the thirty-two marks [of a Great Man].
[He saw] the eighty minor marks; he saw only his disciples and retinue surrounding him as he preached the Dharma;
he saw only the hearing of the six *pāramitās*; he saw only the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha;
he saw only the complete exposition of the meaning of the six *pāramitās*; and he saw only [the Buddha] sitting beneath the Bodhi tree.
One sees only the various bodhisattvas proceeding to the tree of enlightenment and attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
one sees only those who have already attained *abhisambodhi* and turning the wheel of Dharma;
one sees only the countless hundreds of thousands of assemblies of bodhisattvas; one sees only those who shall thus receive the wisdom of *sarvajñatā*; and one sees only their instruction.
They transform sentient beings and purify Buddha-lands;

they hear only the voices of countless Buddhas throughout the ten directions, hearing only that in such-and-such a direction, in such-and-such a land, a Buddha named so-and-so is preaching the Dharma surrounded by several hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas and disciples as his retinue;

they see only the parinirvāṇa of various Buddhas throughout the ten directions, and they see only those who, after a Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, collect his relics and erect stupas made of the seven treasures, making offerings to those stupas with famous flowers and incense.
Kauśika! Such are the dreams of these good sons and good daughters; they see only most excellent and wondrous images.

These good sons and good daughters sleep in peace and wake in peace, their bodies likewise at ease; they are pure and light, having no craving for food or drink, no craving for clothing, and harboring no expectations regarding any offerings.
Kauśika! It is, for example, like a bhikṣu who practices meditation, whose mind is intent on dhyāna and breath-regulation, who does not crave food, and who is content through dhyāna. Why is this?
Because the devas and spirits take the essence of various flavors to augment their vital energy,
the devas and spirits from all the Buddha-lands of the ten directions likewise come to augment him with the essential nutrients of all kinds of food and drink.
The Buddha told Kauśika:

"If good sons or good daughters wish to attain these merits of the present life, they should study this Prajñāpāramitā, copy it, uphold it, and recite it, never allowing their minds to depart from sarvajñatā (all-knowledge)."
Even if these good sons and good daughters are unable to receive and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, unable to recite it or practice its teachings,
yet they merely transcribe it into a scroll, reverently attend to it, and offer worship with incense, flowers, banners, and canopies while taking refuge in it, their merit will be immeasurable.

Furthermore, if one additionally studies, recites, and practices the Prajñāpāramitā, with a mind that never departs from sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), their merit shall surpass the merit of making offerings to all Buddhas in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions.

If there is someone who makes offerings to all the Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions for as long as their life lasts—adorning them with incense, flowers, silken canopies, banners, and streamers, as well as robes and alms bowls—or if, after a Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, they take up his relics and erect a stupa of the seven precious substances to make offerings as previously described; [the merit of the latter is greater].

It is not equal to the merit obtained by a son of good family or a daughter of good family who upholds, recites, studies, and contemplates the matters within this Prajñāpāramitā; their merit exceeds that of the former person who makes offerings by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, and even hundreds of billions of times.
38. Chapter on Relics. The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra, Chapter Thirty-Eight: On Relics. The Buddha addressed Śakra Devānām Indra, saying: “Kauśika!
Suppose there were one portion consisting of the entire bodily relics of a Buddha filling the whole of Jambudvīpa,
and another portion consisting of a written scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā being held and maintained.
"Of these two portions, which would you wish to take?
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
I would rather take the Prajñāpāramitā. Why is this?
It is not that I dare to harbor a sense of pride toward the śarīra, nor that I dare to be disrespectful, nor that I do not wish to make offerings to it.
Because the bodies of all Buddhas are born from the Prajñāpāramitā, the śarīras of all Tathāgatas are likewise worthy of veneration due to the causal conditions of the Prajñāpāramitā.
Śāriputra said to Śakra Devānām Indra: “Kauśika!

This Prajñāpāramitā is supreme and formless; it cannot be guarded or maintained, it is invisible, unimpeded, and of a single characteristic. That which is of a single characteristic is, in fact, without characteristics.”
How should one wish to receive and uphold it?

To uphold this Prajñāpāramitā is to dwell neither in the place of birth, nor in the place of increase or decrease, nor in the place of expectation, nor in the place of non-expectation, nor in the place of transformation, nor in the place of attachment or cessation;
it is neither to uphold the Buddha-dharma as something to be given away, nor to abandon the dharma of ordinary persons.
Nor does one give anything by upholding the precepts and dharmas of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, nor does one abandon the dharmas of ordinary persons;
nor does one give anything by upholding unconditioned dharmas (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*), nor does one abandon conditioned dharmas (*saṃskṛta-dharma*);

nor does one give anything by upholding internal and external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) and the emptiness of existence and non-existence (*bhāvābhāva-śūnyatā*), nor does one give anything by upholding the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, or the dharma of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
"How do you wish to uphold it?
Śakra Devānām Indra replied, "So be it, so be it!"
Śāriputra! There is one who knows this Prajñāpāramitā as neither adding anything to the Buddha-dharmas nor discarding anything from the dharmas of ordinary beings.
One who acts with such knowledge is practicing the mindfulness of Prajñāpāramitā; this is because they enter into the six pāramitās without duality.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One praised Śakra Devānām Indra, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
As you have said, there is no duality in entering the six pāramitās."
Why is this? Because, Kauśika,
the six pāramitās are not dualistic in nature.
The perfection of wisdom and the dharma-nature are not two; the six perfections, the limit of reality, and the inconceivable are also not two.
Śakra Devānām Indra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
All devas and the people of the world should pay homage to the Prajñāpāramitā.”
Why is this? Because it is within the *prajñāpāramitā* that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas realize unexcelled, perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*).
World-Honored One!
For example, it is as when I am together with the sons of gods in the Palace of Equal Excellence, and the sons of gods gather there to pay homage to me.
Even if I am not seated, the sons of gods all pay homage to my seat because it is the place where they receive instruction.
Having circumambulated it once, each departed on their own way.

If a son or daughter of good family writes down and maintains this Prajñāpāramitā, and further explains its meaning to others, then the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas of the ten directions will all pay homage at the place where the Prajñāpāramitā is kept, and having completed their circumambulation, they will depart.

Why is this? It is because all Buddhas and Tathāgatas are born from within it; the peace, security, and happiness of all people in the world are born from within it; and the relics of all Buddhas and the practices of all Bodhisattvas all enter into *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), for they all follow and obey its instructions by virtue of *sarvajñatā*.
For this reason, World-Honored One,
between these two portions, I choose to receive, uphold, and recite the Prajñāpāramitā.
Because I receive and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, even when the Dharma is about to perish, I shall have no fear, nor will I ever entertain such thoughts.
Why is this? Because the Prajñāpāramitā is without marks, without form, and cannot be apprehended.
From the six pāramitās up to sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), all are without marks, without activity, without form, and cannot be seen; this is the markless dharma of the Prajñāpāramitā.
For this reason, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, has attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi within the dharma that is without activity, without attainment, and without marks.
World-Honored One!

Because the Prajñāpāramitā is signless, when one preaches the Dharma for disciples, it is likewise signless, without attainment, and without practice, thereby enabling the realization of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

For this reason, people of the world, as well as devas, spirits, and nāgas, should all serve and revere it, making offerings of exquisite flowers, exquisite incense, silken banners, and flowered canopies to the Prajñāpāramitā.
"World-Honored One!

If there are those who receive, uphold, recite, and practice the Prajñāpāramitā, or who further offer incense, flowers, and other honors to its various scriptural volumes, such persons shall never again fall into the three evil realms, nor shall they fall into the paths of the Arhats or Pratyekabuddhas; until they achieve Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, they shall encounter no such difficulties."

In every birth they shall constantly see the Buddhas and never be separated from the Buddha-fields; passing from one Buddha-field to another, they shall offer incense, flowers, and precious ornaments to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
Even if the entire three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system were filled with the relics of the whole body, between these two treasures, I would nevertheless choose the Prajñāpāramitā.
For what reason,
World-Honored One?
It is because these relics have been born from within the Prajñāpāramitā and thus receive offerings.

Good sons and good daughters, by virtue of this offering, they sever the three evil destinies and attain the blessings of rebirth among devas and humans; according to their respective aspirations within the Dharma of the Three Vehicles, each shall achieve liberation.
World-Honored One!
Having transcribed the Prajñāpāramitā, seeing its scroll is no different from seeing the Buddha himself. Why is this?
World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata and the Prajñāpāramitā are equal, for there is no duality between them.

Just as the World-Honored One has taught through the threefold instruction and the twelve divisions of the scriptures, if there are good sons or good daughters who receive and transcribe the Prajñāpāramitā, uphold its scrolls, and further teach it to others, this is exactly equal and no different from the Buddha’s own teaching. Why is this so?
“World-Honored One!
The Buddha’s threefold teaching and the twelve divisions of the scriptures all emerge from within the Prajñāpāramitā.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!”
And if the Buddhas of the ten directions were to teach the twelve divisions of the scriptures through three matters;
and if there were again a good man or a good woman who taught others using a scroll of the Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra, their merit would likewise be equal and no different.
Why is this? Because the twelvefold scriptures of the Buddhas of the ten directions and the teachings on the three matters are all born from within the Prajñāpāramitā.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!..."

If there are good sons or good daughters who make offerings to as many Buddhas of the ten directions as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River, adorning them with fine robes and all manner of famous flowers;
and if there are others who make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā, their merit and blessings will be no different from those.
Why is this? Because all the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the ten directions have all emerged from within the Prajñāpāramitā.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives and studies the Prajñāpāramitā, reciting, reading, upholding, and practicing its contents, such a person will never fall into the three evil realms, nor will they fall into the stages of the Arhat or Pratyekabuddha; they shall dwell correctly in the stage of Avaivartika.
For what reason?
World-Honored One,
it is because the Prajñāpāramitā is far removed from all maladies.
"Furthermore, World-Honored One!

If there are good men or good women who copy and uphold the Prajñāpāramitā, study, recite, and practice its essential matters, and further make offerings of famous flowers, powdered incense, silken banners, flower canopies, and pennants, you should know that these good men and good women have already been freed from all terrors."
World-Honored One, it is like a person in debt who constantly harbors fear; yet, if he becomes acquainted with a king, he no longer fears.
Why is this? Because he relies upon one who is honorable.
"So it is, World-Honored One!
It is from within the perfection of wisdom that the relics are brought to fulfillment and receive offerings.
World-Honored One!"
One should know that this Prajñāpāramitā is like a king, whereas the relics of the Tathāgata are like debtors; it is by relying on the Prajñāpāramitā that they obtain peace and security.
World-Honored One!
You should know that the wisdom of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge) is entirely accomplished through the prajñāpāramitā; for this reason, among the two treasures, I take up the prajñāpāramitā.
Why is this? The body of the Tathāgata is born from the *prajñāpāramitā*;

the thirty-two marks of a great man, the ten powers of a Buddha, the four fearlessnesses, the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha, and great loving-kindness and great compassion—all are born from the *prajñāpāramitā*.
The five pāramitās also arise from the prajñāpāramitā, thereby each obtaining its own name;
the sarvajñājñāna (all-knowing wisdom) attained by the Tathāgata likewise emerges entirely from within the prajñāpāramitā.
“World-Honored One!

Wherever in this trichiliocosm there are those who receive, uphold, recite, and study this Prajñāpāramitā, and who offer it incense and flowers, serve it, and pay it homage, neither humans nor non-humans shall ever find an opportunity to harm them. These sentient beings shall all, in the future, attain the Dharma of Nirvāṇa.”
World-Honored One!
This Prajñāpāramitā possesses such great majestic power that it causes all sentient beings throughout the trichiliocosm to establish the Buddha-work.
World-Honored One!
Wherever the Prajñāpāramitā resides, one should know that a Buddha has already been present in that place.
For example, wherever a priceless maṇi jewel is located in the world, neither humans nor non-humans can find an opportunity to harm it.
If a man or woman is possessed by a non-human spirit, one should bring this maṇi jewel; when the non-human spirit sees the maṇi jewel, it cannot endure its majesty and will depart spontaneously.
If a man or woman suffers from the illness of alternating chills and fever, and one shows them this maṇi jewel, their illness is immediately cured.
If one holds the maṇi jewel in the darkness, it becomes instantly bright.
When worn during the heat, the place where the maṇi jewel is placed immediately becomes cool;
when worn during the cold, the place where the maṇi jewel is placed immediately becomes warm.
Wherever the maṇi jewel is set, all poisons of malevolent influences are entirely eliminated.
If a man or a woman is bitten by a snake or a viper, upon seeing the maṇi jewel, the poison is immediately removed and the wound heals.
World-Honored One!
Such are the virtues of the maṇi jewel: if a man or a woman suffers from blindness, eye pain, bodily swelling, or sores, upon seeing the maṇi jewel, all such sores and ailments are entirely cured.
World-Honored One!
Such are the virtues of this maṇi jewel.
If it is placed in water, the water immediately takes on the color of the maṇi jewel accordingly.
“World-Honored One!

If one takes various multicolored silks and wraps them within them, placing them in water, the water will continuously take on the color of a maṇi jewel; even turbid water will become clear. Such is the virtue of the maṇi jewel.”
At that time, Ānanda said to Śakra Devānām Indra:
“Kauśika! Is what you have described a maṇi jewel from the heavens?”
"Is this a treasure of the world?
Śakra Devānām Indra replied to Ānanda,
"That which I have spoken of is a treasure of the heavens."

There are also mani-jewels in the world, yet they do not equal the jewels of the heavens; their virtues are incomplete and do not match those of the celestial jewels, for their qualities cannot be compared through any analogy.
Regarding the jewels I have spoken of, whether they are placed within a casket or within a chest, their radiance shines forth.
Even if one were to take the pearl away from that place, the light would continue as before.

Wherever there are those who write down, uphold, receive, and study the Prajñāpāramitā, that place shall be free from the perils of manifold afflictions; that location shall be honored, just like the place where a maṇi jewel resides.

One should know that the *prajñāpāramitā* is like a *maṇi* jewel, its merit being immeasurable. It encompasses the merit of the five *pāramitās* and *sarvajñatā*; the emptiness of the internal and external, as well as the emptiness of existence and non-existence; the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha; the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), suchness (*tathatā*), the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), the inconceivable, and the merit of the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*). After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, his relics receive offerings and service. The wisdom of omniscience arises from the exhaustion of all habitual tendencies; it constantly guards and never forgets the Dharma. This wisdom of omniscience is the vessel for all dharmas.
Therefore, the relics of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, receive honor and worship; for these relics are the precious vessel of the Prajñāpāramitā.

The perfection of non-interruption and non-attachment, the perfection of neither arising nor ceasing, the perfection of neither coming nor going nor abiding—it is for this reason that the relics of the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, receive offerings.
"World-Honored One, the relics are the vessels for the *pāramitās* of all dharmas; because they are composed of the *pāramitās* of all dharmas, the relics receive offerings."
Setting aside these relics of the Tathāgata contained within this trichiliocosm,
even if the relics were to fill as many world-systems as there are grains of sand along the banks of the Ganges, I would nevertheless take up the Prajñāpāramitā.
Why is this so? Because the relics of the Tathāgata all emerge from within it, and thus they receive offerings.

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family makes offerings to the relics, reveres and serves them, they will obtain the blessings of the heavens and the world; they will be born into great clans such as the Kṣatriyas, the Brāhmaṇas, or the Gṛhapatis; they will be born among the foremost of the Four Heavenly Kings, and they will obtain the meritorious blessings of the sixth heaven.
Having planted these roots of merit, one will surely transcend all sufferings by means of those wholesome foundations.

Furthermore, if one upholds this Prajñāpāramitā and makes offerings and serves it, one will then become fully endowed with the five pāramitās, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and the eighteen unique qualities of a Buddha. One will transcend the stages of the Arhat and Pratyekabuddha, abide in the virtues of a Bodhisattva, and immediately attain the supernormal powers (*abhijñā*). Traveling from one Buddha-field to another, one shall teach and transform beings according to their needs, causing each to attain their proper place.

Sometimes he becomes a Cakravartin king, sometimes a Kṣatriya or a Brāhmaṇa, and sometimes a wealthy householder of great lineage; in each case, he instructs them according to their respective customs.
Therefore, World-Honored One!
It is not out of arrogance or a lack of reverence that I fail to serve you, nor is it because I have no desire to receive and uphold your relics.
World-Honored One!
If there are sons or daughters of good family who respectfully serve the Prajñāpāramitā, they have thereby already made offerings to the relics of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.
“World-Honored One!

If one wishes to see the countless Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions, one should practice the Prajñāpāramitā, recite it, receive and uphold it, and teach others to study, practice, and make offerings to it. By doing so, good sons and good daughters shall be able to see the countless Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions.”
Because good sons and good daughters make offerings to the Prajñāpāramitā, they thereby obtain all the Buddha-dharmas.
World-Honored One!
Those good sons and good daughters who wish to see the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the Samyaksaṃbuddhas, should receive, uphold, and recite the Prajñāpāramitā.
World-Honored One!
Furthermore, there are two dharmas. What are these two?
It refers to the dharmas of conditioned phenomena (*saṃskṛta-dharma*) and the dharmas of unconditioned phenomena (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*). What are the dharmas of conditioned phenomena?

They are the wisdom of internal and external emptiness (*adhyātma-bahirdhā-śūnyatā*) and the wisdom of the emptiness of existence and non-existence (*bhāvābhāva-śūnyatā*); the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (*saptatriṃśad-bodhipākṣika-dharma*), the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), the four fearlessnesses (*vaiśāradya*), the ten powers of a Buddha (*daśa-tathāgata-bala*), and the eighteen unique qualities (*āveṇika-dharma*); the wisdom regarding unwholesome and wholesome dharmas, the wisdom regarding outflowing and non-outflowing dharmas, and the wisdom regarding mundane and supramundane dharmas. These are called the dharmas of conditioned phenomena.
What is the dharma of unconditioned dharmas?

It refers to the dharma that is neither born nor extinguished; it neither abides nor does it not abide, being without distinction; it is neither attached to nor severed from; it neither increases nor decreases—the reality of all dharmas.
"What is the reality of all dharmas?
That which is non-existent is the reality of dharmas; this is called the dharma of unconditioned dharmas.
The Buddha addressed Śakra-devānām-indra, saying:

"So it is, so it is! All the Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas of the past attained unexcelled perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) by means of the *prajñāpāramitā*, and their assemblies of disciples likewise each attained their respective stages from *srotāpanna* up to *arhat* and *pratyekabuddha*.
